source_text:
Σύ, δεσποτα, ἔδωκας τὴν ἐξουσίαν τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῖς διὰ τοῦ μεγαλοπρεποῦς καὶ ἀνεκδιηγήτου κράτους σου, εἰς τὸ γινώσκοντας ἡμᾶς τὴν ὑπὸ σοῦ αὐτοῖς δεδομένην δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν ὑποτάσσεσθαι αὐτοῖς, μηδὲν ἐναντιουμένους τῷ θελήματί σου: οἶς δός, κύριε, ὑγίειαν, εἰρήνην, ὁμόνοιαν, εὐστάθειαν. εἰς τὸ διέπειν αὐτοὺς τὴν ὑπὸ σοῦ δεδομένην αὐτοῖς ἡγεμονίαν ἀπροσκόπως.
σὺ γάρ, δέσποτα ἐπουράνιε, βασιλεῦ τῶν αἰώνων, δίδως τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ ἐξουσίαν τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὑπαρχόντων: σύ, κύριε, διεύθυνον τὴν βουλὴν αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ καλὸν καὶ εὐάρεστον ἐνώπιόν σου, ὅπως διέποντες ἐν εἰρήνῃ καὶ πραΰτητι εὐσεβῶς τὴν ὑπὸ σοῦ αὐτοῖς δεδομένην ἐξουσίαν ἵλεώ σου τυγχάνωσιν.
ὁ μόνος δυνατὸς ποιῆσαι ταῦτα καὶ περισσότερα ἀγαθὰ μεθ̓ ἡμῶν, σοὶ ἐξομολογούμεθα διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ προστάτου τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δἰ οὗ σοι ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ μεγαλωσύνη καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς γενεὰν γενεῶν καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: Prayer for rulers and final doxology
orientation: The Roman church is closing its long prayer to God, asking him to give health, peace, harmony, and stability to earthly rulers so that they govern blamelessly, and then offering a final doxology through Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: You, Master, gave the authority of the kingdom to them through your magnificent and indescribable might, so that we, knowing the glory and honor given to them by you, submit to them, in nothing opposing your will; to whom give, Lord, health, peace, harmony, stability, so that they administer the leadership given to them by you without stumbling. For you, heavenly Master, king of the ages, give to the sons of men glory and honor and authority over the things that exist on the earth; you, Lord, make straight their counsel according to what is good and pleasing before you, so that administering in peace and gentleness piously the authority given to them by you, they may obtain your mercy. The only one able to do these things and more abundant good things with us, to you we confess through the high priest and protector of our souls Jesus Christ, through whom to you be the glory and the majesty both now and to generation of generations and to the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: The adjective modifies κράτους (might) and means 'not able to be fully narrated or told out'; 'indescribable' captures the sense of surpassing expression.
The adverb derives from προσκόπτω (to strike against, stumble); it means governing without offense or fault, so 'without stumbling' keeps the literal image.
The verb means to direct or make straight; the imperative asks God to straighten the rulers' counsel, keeping the literal directional image.
The verb means to acknowledge openly or confess; in a doxological context it carries the sense of acknowledging God's glory, so 'we confess' preserves the liturgical force.
The noun means one who stands before or guards, a patron or protector; 'protector' fits the image of Christ guarding souls.

pass_b_english: You, Lord, gave them the authority of the kingdom through your magnificent and indescribable might. You did this so that we, knowing the glory and honor you have given them, would submit to them and in no way oppose your will. Give them, Lord, health, peace, harmony, and stability, so that they may administer the leadership you have given them without stumbling.

For you, heavenly Lord, King of the ages, give to the sons of men glory and honor and authority over the things that exist on the earth. You, Lord, make straight their counsel toward what is good and pleasing before you. Then, as they administer in peace and gentleness with godliness the authority you have given them, they may obtain your mercy.

You alone are able to do these things and even greater good among us. We confess you through the high priest and protector of our souls, Jesus Christ. Through him be glory and majesty to you, both now and from generation to generation and to the ages of ages. Amen.

polish.changed: Broke long sentences into shorter, clearer units; clarified that 'them' refers to earthly rulers; made the prayer's purpose clauses read naturally; kept all content and Scripture references exactly.

problems.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
problems.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

edits.old: For you, heavenly Master, King of the ages
edits.new: For you, heavenly Lord, King of the ages

fixed: Standardized 'Master' to 'Lord' for God in both instances to maintain consistency with the rest of the translation.

last_rejected.quote: We confess you through the high priest and protector of our souls, Jesus Christ.
last_rejected.source_quote: σοὶ ἐξομολογούμεθα διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ προστάτου τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
last_rejected.why: With the dative, ἐξομολογούμεθα means we give thanks or praise to you, not a creedal confession of you.
last_rejected.fix: To you we give thanks through the high priest and protector of our souls, Jesus Christ.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξομολογούμεθα σοι (dative) in 1 Clement 61 means 'we praise/give thanks to you'; 'confess you' is a stilted but near-range rendering, and doxology context keeps the sense of praise.

last_rejected.quote: You, Lord, make straight their counsel toward what is good and pleasing before you.
last_rejected.source_quote: σύ, κύριε, διεύθυνον τὴν βουλὴν αὐτῶν
last_rejected.why: διεύθυνον is an imperative petition. The English reads as an indicative statement, so the prayer becomes a claim.
last_rejected.fix: You, Lord, direct their counsel toward what is good and pleasing before you,
last_rejected.ruling: διεύθυνον is aorist imperative; “You, Lord, make straight” is vocative plus imperative, the normal rendering of σύ, κύριε, διεύθυνον.
